s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus with solid and cystic components
key_facts: Several months of sinus pressure and facial swelling
Several weeks of external deviation of her nasal septum
No significant past medical history
Left nasal mass noted on examination
Mild left-sided proptosis present
CT scan showed a heterogeneous mass in the left maxillary sinus
Mass eroded the orbital floor, medial and posterior maxillary walls, and anterior ethmoid air cells
Displacement of inferior rectus without muscle invasion
Left maxillary alveolar ridge and several molar roots involved
Bony changes showed remodeling and thinning
Biopsy showed spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells
Rare mitotic activity
No cytologic atypia

differentials: Squamous cell carcinoma of the sinus
per_call: Squamous cell carcinoma of the sinus

shortlist.label: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of progressive facial swelling and sinus pressure with nasal septum deviation and proptosis in a teenage patient

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results showing spindle cell process with significant multinucleated giant cells support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Central giant cell granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and radiological features, including bony changes and involvement of the maxillary alveolar ridge, are consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Radiological findings of bony remodeling and thinning, along with the presence of a heterogeneous mass, could be indicative of fibrous dysplasia

shortlist.label: Cherubism
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of a heterogeneous mass with solid and cystic components, along with the clinical features of facial swelling and proptosis, make cherubism a plausible diagnosis
